commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Merge segment reading.

Keep one spare byte after the ciphertext and terminate it when another
PFB segment follows the private dictionary, as the PFA path already does.

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

Read each private segment instead of one contiguous span, and keep the
spare byte used to terminate the dictionary.  When more than one segment
is merged, store a newline in that trailer.

* isrc/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Check the size.

Fixes https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/568035737, also in #1470.
An empty private segment is noted in the trailer byte.

coupling: T1_Get_Private_Dict keeps a single spare byte after the PFB ciphertext (allocation size private_len+1, tracked as alloc_len across segments). Three commits each append one trailer byte through the same tail cursor and none of them enlarges that reservation. c3d48ea remembers the tag that ends the private dictionary and, when it is 0x8001 or 0x8003, stores a NUL at private_len+tail++. cc9c04b reads each segment with one realloc that still reserves exactly one spare byte, counts the segments, and stores a newline at private_len+tail++ when more than one segment was merged. 9a6d987 keeps its size check and stores another NUL at private_len+tail++ when a zero-length private segment was present. One store uses index private_len and stays inside the spare byte. A second store uses private_len+1, one byte past the block. The PoC is a PFB with an empty 0x8002 segment, a 4-byte 0x8002 segment, and a following 0x8001 segment, so all three conditions are true and private_len is 4. Removing any one store leaves the other pair, and that pair still writes past the single spare byte. A one-segment PFB takes only the end-tag store, which fits in the spare byte and does not change private_len, decryption, or the parser limit.
